entry_disclaimer.title: New molecular and imaging findings
entry_disclaimer.body: Liquid biopsies (April–May 2026) have revealed new alterations: ESR1 D538G (endocrine resistance) and RB1 mutations (a predictor of neuroendocrine transformation). The Ga-68 DOTATOC PET-CT confirms multiple bone metastases with somatostatin receptor subtype 2 (SSTR2) overexpression — a new therapeutic target via radioligand therapy (PRRT). The molecular profile has become more complex and reinforces the need to explore the neuroendocrine pathway in parallel with the breast (luminal) one.

home.intro_line: Diagnosed in March 2026 with luminal breast cancer and a neuroendocrine component that does not fit standard protocols.
home.s3_heading: What Spanish protocols don't cover, we cover.
home.s3_subheading: Spanish protocols only account for half of the tumor's biology: they're built for standard HR+ breast cancer, and Miriam's is not.
home.s3_p1: Histologically it is a luminal breast carcinoma (HR+/HER2−). But IHC detected ~80% neuroendocrine differentiation. That second biology is not part of the standard Spanish protocol.
home.s3_p2: Practical result: hormonal treatment covers the breast (luminal) component. The neuroendocrine component, with its own dynamics and targets, is left unaddressed.
home.s3_p3: Oncologists cannot prescribe off-protocol without solid evidence. Generating that evidence requires molecular rebiopsy, advanced panels and international review boards. None of this is funded by public healthcare for a low-frequency case.
home.s3_pet_paragraph: Gallium-68 DOTATOC PET-CT: multiple bone metastases with somatostatin receptor overexpression (subtype 2, SSTR2) and focal uptake in the right breast tail. The tumor expresses a target that breast protocols do not contemplate as standard, opening the radioligand path (PRRT).

home.s8_p1: An {nof1} trial is a clinical trial built for a single patient: treatment is designed around her tumor's actual profile, not an average protocol. That makes it possible to combine drugs to target its two sides at once — the luminal (breast) one and the possible neuroendocrine one.

ciencia.evidence_page_intro: Every hypothesis in this case is grounded in peer-reviewed literature and clinical trials. Here is the evidence behind the therapeutic axes, grouped by theme.
ciencia.evidence_hook_body: The peer-reviewed studies and clinical trials that back each hypothesis in the case —FGFR1, PRRT/SSTR, the neuroendocrine transformation and more— gathered on a dedicated page.
ciencia.proposed_panel_caption: Proposed bone rebiopsy protocol: component, method and core/format, targets and clinical implication
ciencia.axes_note: Hypotheses derived from the molecular profile, not a prescribed treatment. The advanced rebiopsy will confirm or rule them out before defining the N-of-1 strategy.
ciencia.goal_n_of_1_desc: A clinical trial with one patient. Therapeutic decisions are designed on the tumor's actual molecular profile, not on a generic HR+ average. The path: rebiopsy with advanced panel → review at WIN Consortium international MTB → molecularly-directed N-of-1 treatment.
ciencia.win_consortium_desc: WIN Consortium (Worldwide Innovative Network in Oncology) connects precision-oncology centres of excellence to design individualised diagnostic and therapeutic strategies.
ciencia.win_consortium_precedent: A precedent: precision oncology decided on the patient's molecular data, not on the tumor's label.
ciencia.why_no_fit_guidelines: Why doesn't this tumor fit the protocols?
ciencia.why_no_fit_guidelines_text: On paper this is a {luminal} breast cancer (HR+/HER2−). Under the microscope, ~80% of the tumor shows neuroendocrine differentiation, with {fgfr1} and {ccnd1} amplification. Spanish protocols recommend treating it as standard luminal and ignoring the {neuroendocrino} component; yet the WHO has recognized breast neuroendocrine neoplasms as a distinct entity since its 2019 classification, and clinical literature shows this hybrid subtype ({bcned}) has worse prognosis and usually needs different strategies.
ciencia.thesis: The thesis: biology, not the organ of origin, should guide treatment.
ciencia.thesis_goal: Goal: an N-of-1 trial that sets a precedent for precision oncology in ultra-rare subtypes.
ciencia.updates_2026_subtitle: Results generated in 2026 that complement the 2024 primary-tissue profile.
ciencia.ctdna_what: Circulating tumor DNA (ctDNA) from peripheral blood analyzed by NGS. A standard blood draw detects mutations, amplifications and clonal dynamics without a tissue biopsy. Especially useful in bone-only disease, where tissue is scarce or molecularly uninformative.
ciencia.imaging_intro: The tracer reveals an actionable target visible in vivo: the tumour expresses {sstr}, the target of {prrt}. Standard breast-cancer protocols do not consider this route.
ciencia.imaging_what: PET with the 68Ga-DOTATOC radiotracer, which binds mainly the somatostatin receptor subtype 2 (SSTR2). Visualizes in vivo which lesions express SSTR2 and could therefore respond to radioligand therapy (PRRT).
ciencia.article_fallback_notice: This article is not yet available in English. Showing the Spanish version.
ciencia.snapshot_intro: The essentials in ten seconds, before the molecular detail.
ciencia.snapshot_diagnosis: Infiltrating carcinoma (NST) with ~80% neuroendocrine differentiation (BC-NED) · luminal HR+/HER2− · premenopausal · dx January 2024
ciencia.snapshot_resistance: ESR1 D538G · RB1 loss (3 variants in ctDNA) · CDK4/6i resistance
ciencia.snapshot_target: SSTR2+ on Ga-68 PET → radioligand therapy (PRRT) candidate
ciencia.snapshot_status: ECOG 0 · multiple bone metastases (no visceral involvement) · abemaciclib stopped (March 2026)
ciencia.snapshot_grade: ER 95% · PR 5% · HER2 0 (ultralow) · Ki67 60% · G2 (Nottingham) · low TMB and MSI
ciencia.ctdna_dynamics_title: How it evolves in the blood
ciencia.ctdna_dynamics_intro: The tumour isn’t static: ctDNA tracks its changes (VAF) across three plasma draws, with no biopsy needed.
ciencia.app_inline_text: What if you could follow the case over time —the response to each treatment line and how the ctDNA (VAF) shifts between draws— yourself? We are bringing it together in an interactive app.
ciencia.app_hook_body: A dashboard for oncology teams: the full case in a queryable, exportable format (timeline, reports and molecular profile), built for second opinions and tumor boards.

team.title: The team
team.subtitle: One patient, an international team and artificial intelligence, searching for the therapy that standard oncology doesn't yet consider.
team.network_origin_body: A scientific and technological research association (biotech, AI, data). We're getting it ready. In the meantime, you can help the case:
notus_list: We do not promise cures. We document biological hypotheses and their real probabilities.
We do not use “fight” or “warrior” language. We talk biology, data and clinical decisions.
We do not replace the medical team. We add external analysis; clinical decisions are signed by Miriam's oncology team.
We do not publish clinical data without review. Transparency demands rigor, not speed.
We're not a perfect AI. The AI we use sometimes hallucinates — and the humans reviewing it do too. If you spot a typo, let us know.
team.how_it_formed: This team wasn't planned — it came together organically. People from technology, medicine, AI and research saw a case that moved them and decided to contribute what they know. There's no hierarchy and no spotlight-seeking: each person advises and supports from their own field. There's a single shared goal: to let the biology of this tumor guide the treatment. Clinical decisions always remain with Miriam's doctors.

historia.fallback_notice: This chapter is not yet available in English. Showing the Spanish version.
historia.pending_notice: This is the most personal part of the site, and it's being written by someone who knows Miriam closely: who she is beyond cancer, what she did, and why she does what she does. It'll be ready very soon. Meanwhile, you can follow the day-to-day on her social channels or get to know the case in The science.
historia.story_teaser_1: Three years ago, Miriam was working full-time as a software developer and creating content about technology. Within a matter of months, her life took a radical turn.
historia.story_teaser_2: It all began with back pain, physiotherapy sessions and GPs who couldn't find a solution. As the pain persisted and she wasn't getting answers, she decided to arrange an MRI scan herself. One Thursday in January 2024, she found the test results in her inbox: “probable vertebral metastases”. A couple of weeks later, the definitive diagnosis arrived: “Stage IV breast cancer with neuroendocrine differentiation”.
historia.story_teaser_3: For two years, Miriam has been rebuilding her life piece by piece with treatments that have given her time and peace of mind, but with an end date. In 2026, everything has moved forward at breakneck speed. What if these advances, combined with the specific nature of her cancer, opened doors that previously seemed closed?
historia.story_teaser_4: In this story, we want to tell you about Miriam's case, her journey and her daily routine so that you can truly understand what it means to live with stage 4 cancer.

expenses.title: Where the money goes
expenses.subtitle: Radical transparency: every euro, documented.
expenses.intro: Every euro raised is assigned to a concrete line item and documented here. This is the full breakdown of what the money can go to, in whatever order is needed.
expenses.cost_vs_goal: The first goal's €40,000 covers the first stage; the full range is funded in phases.
expenses.rebiopsy_intro: The centrepiece of the campaign is a single bone biopsy: everything current science allows is extracted from it today, and the rest is preserved so it can be analysed for 10+ years. Its cost splits into two blocks.
expenses.rebiopsy_now_desc: Broad sequencing, expression, functional proteomics, single-cell and organoids on the freshly obtained tissue.
expenses.rebiopsy_bank_desc: Frozen, OCT and live tissue properly stored for new analyses as science advances.
expenses.rebiopsy_value: One procedure, not several: each preserved format avoids having to biopsy again in the future.
expenses.rebiopsy_note: Indicative figures, under review with the labs. Final amounts will be published in the monthly expense report.
expenses.faq_q1: How do I know the money goes to this?
expenses.faq_a1: Every euro is assigned to one of the line items above and will be documented in a monthly expense report we'll publish on this very page. Nothing is diverted outside the case.
expenses.faq_q2: What if more is raised than expected?
expenses.faq_a2: Funds follow the order of priorities: first the rebiopsy and treatment, then monitoring and the analyses the tumour comes to require. Any surplus is kept intact for the case's future medical needs.
expenses.faq_q3: Is donating safe? Is there a receipt?
expenses.faq_a3: Yes. Donations are processed through GoFundMe with secure payment, and you can request a receipt by getting in touch.
expenses.faq_q4: Can I help without donating money?
expenses.faq_a4: Absolutely. Sharing helpmiriam.com with the right oncologist, researcher or patient can be as decisive as a donation.
expenses.faq_a4_link: See all the ways to help
expenses.faq_help: Have another question or want a receipt?
expenses.note: The monthly expense report will be published here as soon as spending begins. We're working to show it as soon as possible.
